name: Woodland (Sam Houston's home)

location.text: Sam Houston State University campus, Huntsville, Walker County, Texas

dates.altered: Used as a boarding house for Sam Houston Normal Institute students in the 1890s; restored 1929 and again through the twentieth and twenty-first centuries; photographs in the Sam Houston Memorial Museum collection show the house 'without the porch'.
dates.note: Three statements, none edited to agree. Wikipedia: 'Built in stages beginning about 1847'. The Texas Historical Commission's 1962 Recorded Texas Historic Landmark marker: 'He and his wife Margaret (Lea) built this house, "Woodland", in 1847 to provide themselves with a town place.' East Texas History: 'The house was finished in February 1848.' The node's own exemplar carries 1847.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 74002097; added to the National Register and designated a National Historic Landmark May 30, 1974 (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
refs.note: Read from the infobox, not from the National Register's own database. The infobox gives the architectural style as 'Dog-trot'.

refs.title: Woodland (Huntsville, Texas) - Wikipedia
refs.note: 'It is a classic dogtrot house, with a central breezeway flanked by rectangular log chambers, with brick chimneys at the ends. A shed-roof porch extends in front of the breezeway, supported by square posts. The breezeway includes a winding staircase which provides access to loft spaces used as bedrooms.'

refs.title: Woodland, Home of Sam Houston -- Texas Historical Commission Atlas, Recorded Texas Historic Landmark marker No. 8482 (1962)
refs.note: The marker text states the construction: 'The house was built in a style common to the South at the time: squared logs covered with hand-hewn, whitewashed boards. The detached kitchen and law office were built of unfinished, squared logs.'

refs.title: Woodland Home | East Texas History
refs.note: 'The house was finished in February 1848'; the family lived on the property eight years and the house was sold in 1858 for $4,000 to pay campaign debts.

note: No HABS survey was found. The type is stated by two independent sources -- the National Register style field ('Dog-trot') and Wikipedia's description of a central breezeway between rectangular log chambers with end chimneys -- and the breezeway stair the description names is the detail the corpus's own dogtrot prose does not mention: the winding stair to the loft stands IN the passage, which makes the passage circulation as well as a room.
